headline: China's internet regulator has drafted rules that would require companies to get a person's consent before using their image or likeness in AI-made digital human content.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 4: the draft was released on 3 April 2026 and its comment period closed on 6 May 2026, so this is older news re-dated.
importance_line: Actors, influencers and ordinary people whose faces and voices are copied are affected first, then AI video studios and short-drama platforms such as Hongguo, but this is only a draft from April and insiders say proving AI copying is hard.
summary: Sixth Tone reports that the Cyberspace Administration of China, the country's internet regulator, released draft rules on digital virtual human services (AI-made digital people and likenesses) on 3 April 2026 after actors and influencers complained their likenesses were used without permission in AI short dramas; the draft would require consent, from parents for minors, and deletion of personal data if consent is withdrawn. This is older news: the public comment period named in the article ended on 6 May 2026, the piece describes only a draft, and an industry insider it quotes says proving that AI copied a voice is often a matter of degree rather than a clear yes or no.
notes: Older news re-dated: the article gives the release date as April 3 and comments open until May 6 (2026 by context: it cites the first quarter of 2026 and a drama released 'earlier this year'). Google News listings show DataGuidance (6 Apr 2026), Biometric Update (8 Apr 2026) and Digital Watch Observatory (7 May 2026, 'China closes consultation on digital virtual human services') - titles only, not read. Whether final measures have been issued since is not known from what was read. Status REPORTED because only Sixth Tone's text was read.
